title: Finite reduction of the direct-image Roos limit for arbitrary inputs
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, schemes X,Y and any morphism f:X→Y. For arbitrary K in the unbounded derived category of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf on X [def-weil-derived-direct-image], suppose the product of sfDirectImageTerm(f,K) exists and let L be any SfIntegralDirectImage(f,K), with its specified Roos projection [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For every n≥0, the actual projection adjunct sfDirectImageReductionComparison(f,L,n) is an isomorphism. No completeness of K, constructibility, geometric base or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Lemmas 3.5.4--3.5.7 and 6.5.11(3); Stacks Tags 0941 and 099N. The completion-unit transport is written by B7.

proof.text: Choose a coefficient reduction calculus S. The total limit Khat of S.reduction(K) is complete, and the counit on S.reduction(K) is invertible by unrestricted normalized reconstruction. The adjunction triangle shows that reduction of the completion unit a:K→Khat is invertible. Naturality of reductionEvaluation then makes every finite scalar extension of a invertible.

proof.text: Apply finite direct image and completed restriction to these isomorphisms. Naturality of sfDerivedRestrictionComparison and sfDerivedReductionTransition proves that they form an isomorphism of the two finite-image towers. Transport the prescribed Roos triangle along this tower isomorphism while retaining its limit object.

proof.text: Convert completeness of Khat to IsSfDerivedComplete. Apply the complete-input direct-image reduction theorem to the transported triangle. Naturality of the scalar adjunction identifies each new projection adjunct with the old one followed by the finite-image isomorphism. Cancel that isomorphism.

    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E X))

    (L : SfIntegralDirectImage l E f K) (n : ℕ) :
